title: Praia march against current government policies
location: Praia, Santiago; route from Praça Alexandre Albuquerque through central Praia to the Government Palace and National Assembly
organizer: Rede das Associações Comunitárias e Cívicas da Praia
participants_original: ASEMANA describes thousands of people participating, including thousands at the National Assembly; a speaker separately says even 100 people can convey a message, not that this was the observed count.
threshold_50_evidence: The contemporary report repeatedly describes thousands participating, a qualitative estimate that exceeds 50 without supplying a numeric bound. It separately quotes a speaker using 100 hypothetically to discuss the message of a small demonstration, not as an attendance estimate.

start_date.summary: The article is dated 5 January 2023 and says the march began that day about 16:30.

end_date.summary: The same-day report follows the gathering to the National Assembly and says participants remained there until around 18:00; exact ending time is not established.

location.summary: The reported route runs from Praça Alexandre Albuquerque through Praia to the Government Palace and National Assembly.

scope.summary: The documented assembly took place along a route in Praia; a broader geographic scope is not established.

organizer.summary: The report identifies the Praia network of community and civic associations as the promoter.

state_target.summary: The report explicitly says the march protested current MpD-government policies and quotes demands about government transparency and public priorities.

demands.summary: The report records government transparency and political-administration complaints, calls to remove the government, and demands for equal pay and decent work.

participants_original.summary: ASEMANA reports thousands participating, including at the National Assembly; the number is qualitative.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Repeated qualitative descriptions of thousands support the threshold; no numeric minimum or maximum is derived.

protester_violence.summary: The report says the demonstration was peaceful and orderly.

state_response.summary: Security forces guarded the Government Palace and blocked Assembly entry, but the report does not establish dispersal or other listed responses; coded unknown pending review.

notes: The article reports slogans about government removal, corruption, justice, hunger, employment and services. At around 17:40 the march reached the Assembly; protesters lay down in front of the security presence until around 18:00. This is one publisher's account, not independent corroboration. The security cordon and entrance blockade are described without an explicit statement that protesters were dispersed.
open_questions: Seek independent contemporary coverage and any organizer record.
Review original codebook rules for this multi-demand march and local scope.
Clarify whether the reported security cordon and blocked Assembly entrance meet the original crowd-dispersal coding rule.

title: Praia municipal-guard strike reported to start 23 January
location: Praia municipality; a concentration was reportedly planned for Praça Alexandre Albuquerque, but actual occurrence is unverified.
organizer: Sindicato dos Trabalhadores do Comércio e Serviços (STCS)
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. Search-result snippets describe a work stoppage but give no number of people at a public gathering. Do not substitute the number of workers or persons affected.

start_date.summary: The search result reports a 23 January start for the strike and a planned concentration that day; body and actual assembly occurrence remain unverified.

location.summary: A native search result, not the retrieved article body, reports a planned concentration at Praça Alexandre Albuquerque in Praia.

organizer.summary: The search result attributes the decision to strike to guards represented by the STCS.

state_target.summary: Search snippets describe failed conciliation with the municipal government and a municipal response about the workers’ demands; bodies were not retrieved.

demands.summary: A search snippet attributes to the municipality a description of unresolved promotion, progression, fines and uniform issues. These claims remain snippet-only.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Neither snippet provides an attendance count or establishes that a public assembly occurred.

notes: A Nação’s 23 January snippets describe a strike beginning that day and a three-day duration, with a second article quoting the municipality. Both A Nação pages returned native-tool cache misses on exact-URL body attempts. No HTTP status was observed, so these are technical retrieval failures, not publisher denials. This is a labor-action lead only; a work stoppage or affected workforce does not itself establish a qualifying public assembly or 50 attendees. A fuller search result reports a planned concentration at Praça Alexandre Albuquerque, but this is only a search snippet and no actual assembly or attendance is verified.
open_questions: Verify from accessible contemporaneous reporting whether the strike actually began and how long it lasted.
Find whether workers formed a public assembly and establish attendance; do not infer assembly size from workforce size.
Verify workers’ demands and municipal response from an accessible original document or independent report.
Verify whether the planned concentration at Praça Alexandre Albuquerque actually occurred and whether 50 or more people attended.

title: Marxa Cabral 2023, planned in Praia and simultaneously on Sal
location: Planned Praia route from the Fundação Amílcar Cabral at Plateau to the memorial at Várzea; BUALA also says the edition would be organized simultaneously on Sal, where venue is unknown.
organizer: Associação Pilorinhu with the Movimento Federalista Pan-Africano and youth/community partners; recurring march linked to Movimentu Korenti di Ativista Rizistensia i Liberdadi.
participants_original: A 16 January Lusa preview anticipates dozens of young people in Praia. The 18 January BUALA account gives no count; neither source reports post-event attendance.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. A pre-event Lusa preview says “dozens” without a number; the BUALA description provides no count. No actual attendance or 50-person assembly has been verified.

start_date.summary: The 16 January preview says the annual 11th edition was planned for Friday, 20 January; occurrence is unconfirmed.

location.summary: The Lusa preview gives a Praia route from Plateau to the memorial in Várzea; BUALA says the edition would also be organized simultaneously on Sal, without a venue.

organizer.summary: The Lusa preview links the recurring march to the activist movement; BUALA describes Associação Pilorinhu, the Movimento Federalista Pan-Africano and youth/community partners for the 2023 edition.

state_target.summary: BUALA frames the march as a political public space for dignity, recognition, resistance and democracy, with critique of the political elite and a roundtable on language politics. Whether these aims target specific domestic state policy under the original codebook remains open.

demands.summary: The Lusa preview records a request to value Cabral’s legacy and a complaint about school treatment; BUALA describes political reflection on language, dignity, recognition and resistance. The exact target policy is not specified.

participants_original.summary: Only the pre-event Lusa preview anticipates dozens; BUALA provides no attendance estimate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Neither source reports actual attendance. The qualitative expectation “dozens” does not establish 50 participants.

scope.summary: BUALA explicitly describes simultaneous organization on Sal alongside the Praia march. Whether to treat these as one nationally coordinated event or separate local episodes remains for coordinator review.

notes: Santiago Magazine marks its 16 January preview SM/Lusa, so Lusa copies are same-origin. The 18 January BUALA text by Redy Wilson Lima describes a four-day program culminating in a street march; it also says the event would be organized simultaneously on Sal. Neither is a post-event report. Keep the planned 20 January start tentative until occurrence and threshold are confirmed.
open_questions: Find post-20 January evidence that the public march occurred and establish actual attendance.
Clarify whether the simultaneous Praia/Sal actions form one coordinated event or separate episodes under the original codebook.
Confirm the state target and specific policy demand; the event is both cultural remembrance and political reflection.
Confirm the month ownership if the four-day program included a qualifying gathering before 20 January.
